claim: Half Heuslers are semiconducting at VEC = 18.
supporting_text: PRIMARY SOURCE READ (data/pdfs/inbox/1-s2.0-S0079678611000021-main.pdf). Verbatim, Section 8: 'As explained in Section 6.2.1, Half-Heusler materials with 18 valence electrons exhibit semiconducting properties.' Supports the claim exactly as written. The mechanism is given earlier: 'In this simplified model they become stable closed shell ions, i.e. a d10 configuration for Y and a s2p6 configuration for Z. This procedure requires 18 valence electrons... Due to the closed shell configuration, Half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons are particularly stable. Changing the valence electron number to a different value mostly causes the compounds to become magnetic and crystallize in a different crystal structure.' The same source ALSO supports our rare-earth counting convention: 'the family of RE PdBi materials, in which Pd contributes ten valence electrons, the RE metal three and Bi five, respectively, which again sums up to 18 valence electrons.' Note the paper records MnNiSb as a 22-electron half-Heusler exception, consistent with our softened wording.

claim: Solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation from first principles has been applied to the half-Heusler space at scale to identify compounds with unusually low conductivity.
supporting_text: PARTLY VERIFIED -- read the citing sentence carefully. Abstract: 'An efficient computational approach using MACHINE-LEARNING TECHNIQUES finds a much larger range of conductivity than expected for an impressive number of half-Heusler compounds.' The work combines first-principles transport with an ML screen. Citing it for 'the BTE applied across the half-Heusler space' is defensible, but the Introduction then presents ML surrogates as the RESPONSE to BTE cost, and this source already did both. Consider acknowledging that, or citing a purely first-principles high-throughput study instead.

Supports both the cost claim and the surrogate-search claim, in half Heuslers specifically.
